newsitem.title: MEXICO: IFC, GIRSA reach $155 mln financing deal.
newsitem.headline: IFC, GIRSA reach $155 mln financing deal.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) said Wednesday it has signed an agreement for a $155 million financing package with GIRSA SA de CV, the chemical products subsidiary of DESC SA de CV, a major Mexican holding company.

"IFC's investment supports a capital expenditure program designed to improve GIRSA's competitiveness and minimize the environmental impact of the company's operations," the IFC said in a news release.
The IFC is an arm of the World Bank that lends money to private-sector projects in developing countries.
In this case the IFC package conists of two loans for its own account: an eight-year, $30 million term loan and a 10-year, $10 million income-participating loan.
In addition, there are two loans for the account of the participants: a seven-year, $40 million syndicated loan and a three-year, $75 million U.S. commercial paper (USCP) facility.
The USCP facility is supported by a syndicated letter of credit provided by Societe Generale. Citicorp acted as co-arranger of the letter of credit portion of the syndication, the IFC said.

The GIRSA program aims to recycle waste heat to increase energy efficiency and construct new facilities that will minimize the inland transport of hazardous chemicals and help reduce air pollution, the IFC said.
